q99_9_location_support.interpretation: The frozen conditional residual-tail masks locate generated extremes well; failure is not missing tail locations. Even zeroing a much broader positive residual excess leaves an overpowered centered body after transported ranks are coupled to the query backbone.

scientific_conclusion: The V41 object-amplitude predictor is supported on the frozen held-out objects in every domain under the predeclared bias, RMSE, and rank-correlation thresholds. Refitting that target is not justified.

The q99.9 conditional residual tail correctly contains essentially every top-three generated-density voxel and about 91 to 93 percent of the top 26. The V42 failure is therefore not caused by failing to locate the generated extremes.

No domain reaches the required 90 percent target bracket fraction even when the positive excess above the train-only conditional q90 threshold is set identically to zero. The q90 zero-excess endpoint remains above the predicted target by a median 0.59, 0.52, and 0.16 dex in TNG100, SIMBA, and Swift.

Coarse and native donor-rank transport must be retired. It couples a donor residual body to the query backbone in a way that cannot be repaired by a positive monotone tail scale while preserving the stochastic body.

The next generator may not perform spatial donor-rank rearrangement. It must learn a train-only local conditional residual likelihood directly at the query location, retain an explicit stochastic innovation, and be judged against the unchanged V6 field and Q3/Q4 gates.
